title: Rochdale Metrolink patrols target knife crime during Sceptre week
excerpt: Police say 381 items were surrendered through knife amnesty bins in Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale during the latest Operation Sceptre campaign.
body:
Police say 381 items were surrendered through knife amnesty bins in Heywood, Middleton and Rochdale during the latest national campaign against knife crime.

Greater Manchester Police published the results on Thursday 26 November after Operation Sceptre ran from 16 to 22 November. The force said the Rochdale district total included 309 knives, daggers, swords, axes and knuckle dusters.

GMP did not provide a breakdown of the remaining surrendered items or say how many of the week's arrests were made in Rochdale borough.

Across Greater Manchester, officers reported 46 arrests, 92 weapon sweeps, visits or engagement with 61 retailers and the recovery of 30 weapons. The force-wide figures are separate from the 381 items GMP said were surrendered through the three Rochdale district amnesty bins.

The results follow patrols carried out by police community support officers on the Metrolink between Newbold and Rochdale town centre. PCSO Tyler Davies, from Rochdale Town Centre's neighbourhood team, confirmed the local patrols in a police community alert published on 17 November.

Operation Sceptre combines enforcement with prevention, education and community engagement. GMP said its school engagement officers work with schools across Greater Manchester on knife crime prevention, including support for teachers through the Pol-Ed education platform.

Detective Superintendent Rich Thompson said police could not tackle knife crime alone and thanked partner organisations for supporting the campaign.

He said: "While last week's results are reassuring, we know there is still a lot more to be done to rid our communities of knife crime, and we will not rest while lives are being lost."

GMP said serious violent crime offences across Greater Manchester were down by 7% and knife-enabled serious violent crime was down by 35%. The force's notes say those comparisons are between the third quarters of 2024/25 and 2025/26. No Rochdale-specific percentage was supplied.

The force said unwanted knives can be handed in safely at a police station. It also encouraged people to report where knives are hidden or seek help if they are concerned that a friend or family member may be carrying one.

GMP also held an online question and answer session on 16 November covering safe knife disposal and support for young people. The questions and answers remain available at https://app.sli.do/event/mPTtysYyVsSfUCZKNaxEmE/live/questions.
